items.rationale: The model keeps nothing between calls, so the program re-sends the whole stack (instructions, tools, question, earlier tool calls and results) plus the newest result. Answers a and d assume the model remembers or looks things up itself.

Call 1 reads 2,000. Call 2 reads 2,000 + 100 + 1,000 = 3,100. Call 3 reads 3,100 + 100 + 1,000 = 4,200. Total 2,000 + 3,100 + 4,200 = 9,300. An answer of 4,200 counts only the final window and misses that every call re-reads the stack.

A new session starts with an empty window, so a fact must be saved outside the window and loaded back in. A larger window (a) does not carry anything across sessions, and the model does not learn from chats on its own (c).

items.answer: Re-sending the whole manual costs tokens on every call, and the model recalls details less reliably in a crowded window (context rot).
accepted: It costs far more to re-read the whole manual on every call.
A huge window makes the model less accurate at finding details.
Too much text hurts recall and raises cost; fewer relevant chunks are cheaper and more accurate.
Because the pages are billed on every call
items.rationale: Either reason is full credit: cost (the stack is re-read and billed on every call) or quality (context rot). Fitting in the window is not a reason to include it.

Used tool results are bulky and no longer needed, so clear them; the booking confirmation is a decision later steps rely on, so keep it. Deleting it (a, d) loses a decision, and keeping everything (b) leaves the window full.
